answer: An agent marketplace can require each active identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days, making its trading garden less of an oasis for sybil swarms. Creating a thousand agents then requires a thousand bonds, tying up capital even at the zenith of demand. If an agent signs conflicting commitments for the same job, anyone can submit both signatures to slash its bond. The attacker pays for every identity and loses collateral when caught equivocating.
